_comment: local_classify cases. The gold labels live in data, not prose.
Three mechanisms, doing three different jobs — and round 3 shipped two of them conflated:
expect_row.category — is the answer CORRECT, independent of how it was worded. The
server has already matched the reply onto the caller's list, so
this survives decoration ('Category: bug' still yields bug).
category_member     — did the model answer with a BARE label as instructed.
label_is            — correct AND bare, conjoined. Useful when you want both at once;
NOT the accuracy signal, because a right answer that was decorated
fails it identically to a wrong one.
Round 3 used label_is for accuracy and then told readers that label_is and
category_member separate 'right but undisciplined' from 'disciplined but wrong'. Since
gold is always one of the categories and both applied the same normalization, label_is
passing IMPLIED category_member passing — the combination readers were told to look for
was unreachable. Accuracy now comes from the server's matched label instead.

cases.why: Issue #1 records this exact failure: a 0.6B model classified 'the effect size was too small and it disappeared after two weeks' as POSITIVE. The sentiment is negative and stated plainly; only the academic register is neutral. This is the regression case the issue asks for.

arguments.text: The effect size was too small and it disappeared after two weeks.

human_review: Issue #1 observed a 0.6B answering `positive` here. label_is now decides that; what is left for you is whether a wrong answer was a near miss (neutral) or an inversion (positive).
If category_member failed while label_is passed, the model was right but decorated its answer.

cases.why: The tool's prompt says 'Reply with the category name alone, copied exactly as written above.' Small models decorate ('Category: bug', 'I would say bug.'). The server matches decorated replies back onto the list, so `matched` stays true — which is why raw_response, not category, is what gets checked here.

arguments.text: The app crashes on launch whenever the config file is missing.

human_review: Compare `text` (the raw reply) with `category` (what the server matched it to). A gap is decoration the caller never asked for — and it now shows as category_member FLAG while row.category stays green, which is the 'right but undisciplined' combination.
This is the case where a 0.6B answered `feature request`: correct-looking row, wrong answer, until the gold label was in data.

cases.why: Issue #1: 'Whether matched: false fires when it should.' Nothing in the offered list fits, so a well-behaved model has no honest bare label to give. The expectation is a ROW fact (matched must be false), not a text fact — scoring it with category_member pointed the verdict backwards: the desired outcome failed and forcing a label passed.
human_review: A forced label that matches is WORSE than an unmatched reply: it looks clean and is wrong. That is now a mechanical failure rather than a note.

LIMIT: the server's `matched` is substring CONTAINMENT (`handleClassify` uses localizedCaseInsensitiveContains), so an honest refusal that names the options — 'neither a bug nor a feature request' — scores matched:true and FLAGs here. That reply is arguably better than 'none', and this check cannot tell them apart. Read `text` before believing this FLAG.
